output.subject: Your mortgage closing and underwriting concerns
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us, and congratulations on buying your first home. We understand how stressful this must be with your closing so close.

You told us that your closing is scheduled for 10/9 and that your rate lock expires on 10/4/2026. You mentioned that your loan officer has not returned your calls or emails for a week. You also said underwriting keeps asking for the same documents, and that you have now uploaded your tax returns three times. You explained that if the closing date is missed, you stand to lose your $15,000 deposit. We're sorry for the worry and frustration this has caused.

You've asked for help getting underwriting completed before your closing, and for someone at the bank who will respond to you. We have shared your message with our Mortgage Servicing team, who will review your concerns, including the dates you've given us. We will respond within 10 business days.

If there is anything else you'd like us to know in the meantime, please reply to this email.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Time-critical: the rate lock expires 10/4/2026 and closing is 10/9. A 10-business-day response may come after both dates, so decide whether faster contact is needed.
The customer gave a cell number and may expect a call. Decide whether to phone them in addition to sending this email.
Check the status of the loan file and confirm whether the tax returns were received each time they were uploaded.
Look into the loan officer's responsiveness and decide whether to assign an alternate contact.
Decide what, if anything, to say about extending the rate lock or about the closing timeline.
The $15,000 deposit risk is the customer's account. Do not imply the bank will cover any loss unless that has been decided.
The draft names the owning team as Mortgage Servicing per intake. Confirm this is the right team for a loan still in underwriting, rather than origination or lending.
